candidates.label: Acute spontaneous bacterial empyema (infected hepatic hydrothorax) in a patient with Child-Pugh C cirrhosis
missing_or_uncertain: distinction between primary and secondary infection

candidates.label: Community-acquired pneumonia with parapneumonic effusion progressing to empyema
Malignant pleural effusion with secondary bacterial infection in the setting of chronic myeloid leukemia
Tuberculous empyema with superimposed bacterial infection

response.rationale: The record shows a chronic right pleural effusion (1 year) in a patient with decompensated cirrhosis, plus acute unstable vital signs, marked leukocytosis, elevated CRP, positive cultures from pleural fluid and blood, and CT evidence of empyema that resolved on follow-up. This strongly supports infected hepatic hydrothorax (spontaneous bacterial empyema). Other diagnoses like pneumonia or malignancy are less consistent with the chronic effusion and the specific resolution of empyema, while uninfected hydrothorax is contradicted by positive cultures and inflammatory markers.
